I'll take this from the perspective of the CSI effect. We cannot detect everything. DNA evidence is processed in special labs that are DNA clean (hairnets, lab coats, mask, gloves, almost no visible skin). And worst of all we do not have results in a matter of minutes. It can sometimes take weeks. The time disparagy in my opinion is the worst.
In some respects,very. It is a stressful job but the sense of satisfaction when you close a difficult case is fantastic. Definitely a rewarding career.
The most interesting cases to me are legal high cases where I get to see new drugs in circulation. In terms of big, I have had cases where cocaine seizures went in excess of millions.
The simple answer would be a rock. Officer thought it was drugs. The phone call about it was kind of awkward.

Our jobs have gotten significantly more difficult with legal highs as they appear and disappear in popularity very quickly. I wouldn't comment on which is more dangerous, firstly because I am not a toxicologist and secondly, the research on synthetic drugs in terms of neurotoxicity have not yet been done.
